notes: scan046.N1: The page begins with (3), X_{Delta_0} → X, and says hypothesis a) makes this morphism finite, explained as proper, separated and with finite fibres; it is also called a local immersion. The content of hypothesis a) is not supplied on this page. These assertions were carried as background without independent verification.

scan046.N2: A targeted structural check follows directly from (4) and (5). Each Gamma_{ij} is the graph of X_i → X_j, hence its first projection identifies that graph with X_i. For a fixed target component X_i under the first projection, the disjoint-union source consists of one such copy for each j≥i. Thus that restriction is a constant disjoint-union covering with indexing fibre I_i={j in I | j≥i}. The order condition in (4) matches the displayed I_i formula. This checks the graph/fibre description, not every geometric hypothesis of the page.

scan046.N3: The second graph projection is the inclusion X_i → X_j on each summand. The asserted local-immersion property therefore depends on the geometric status of these inclusions, which was not reconstructed from another page. Likewise the geometric étale/finite terminology and the claimed closedness of (4) were not independently proved here; no local contradiction was found.

scan046.N4: M0971 is sigma directly from its lower loop and distinct right-projecting upper cap. M0970 is less explicit in isolation, but the sentence saying the two projections have respectively the following properties explicitly identifies it with the first projection in (7). Its oval permits sigma, so this same-page notation link resolves M0970 to sigma at medium confidence. The decision does not appeal to a conventional preferred name for a projection.

scan046.N5: In (4), déf is to the right of a vertical two-stroke equality. The draft removes C’s swapped TikZ label placement. Formula numbers (4) and (6) occupy their own left columns so the objects and vertical relation align beneath the written objects. In (7), continuation text is aligned under the predicate on the right, as written. These alignment refinements do not add content; only the wrong side of déf is counted as a C diagram correction.

scan046.N6: The opening straight quotation before graphe has no written closer. The explanatory parenthesis in (7)a opens before en fait constant and has no written closer on this page. No closing marks are supplied. H’s pièce, closing parenthesis after the insertion, dash before en fait, and commas after constant and the set formula are absent from the ink.

scan046.N7: Both insertion leaders were traced separately from their words. Séparé attaches before et, after propre. Sur chaque X_i attaches after constant, before de fibre. Neither leader is a strike-through, comma, parenthesis, or additional mathematical arrow. The only genuine deletion is the tentative parenthetical (que).

scan046.N8: Whole page and both supplied full-resolution halves were read once, including agreed words, every arrow end and label, all product/coproduct indices and handwritten numerals. Twenty body text/formula-object rows were counted, excluding separate connecting strokes and treating interlinear insertions separately in the inventory. Fourteen saved crops were inspected once each. No OCR, outside research, other page inputs, or TeX compilation was used.
